mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% signals active monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 8.0% for two consecutive months indicates labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 8.0% for two consecutive months, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signal weakening demand, depressing corporate revenue growth and generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS decline for two consecutive months, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: In low inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL < 2.0%), a decline in federal funds rate signals active monetary easing that supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL < 2.0%, a decline in FEDFUNDS is followed by negative S&P 500 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates real economy contraction, reducing corporate profits and generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO declines, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Residential construction permits (HOUST) exceeding 700.0 for two consecutive months signals strong housing market activity, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST exceeds 700.0 for two consecutive months, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and declines in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicate labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE increases and PAYEMS declines for two consecutive months, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: In high industrial production regimes (INDPRO > 100), a decline in manufacturing output signals supply chain disruption, reducing corporate operational efficiency and generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO > 100, a decline in INDPRO is followed by positive S&P 500 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.
